terms.gloss: a problem to be solved, a question
terms.comment: Solve a problem: quaestiōnem solvere (Sen., Quint.).

terms.gloss: a problem set for solving, a puzzle
evidence: Traupman 364: problēma, a problem in mathematics
terms.comment: The Greek word, in Suetonius and Gellius (Lewis & Short: post-Augustan).

phrases.english: Did you solve this problem by yourself?

sources: Lewis & Short: quaestio · Lewis & Short: problema
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 364.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
